review.json's stamp was confirmed fresh (node scripts/check-stamp-freshness.mjs review.json => status: fresh) both before and after this run's own read-only pytest/vitest executions; spec.json and red.json were already reported stale by review.md itself (Warning 1) -- per this stage's own staleness rules those two are advisory only and do not affect this run.

This is the first security-checker run for this repository (no prior .pipeline/security-history/ entries exist); every observation is FIRST_OBSERVATION and every coverage_transition is NOT_COMPARABLE. No trend/regression claim is made anywhere in this report.

The CH-05 WebSocket gateway subscriber does not exist yet (spec.md explicitly excludes services/gateway/**); every WS-* check that depends on a WebSocket handshake/subscription is NOT_APPLICABLE because that half of the surface is genuinely ABSENT, not because it was skipped.

MCPT-09 (ephemeral-credential issuance: entropy/hashing/one-time disclosure) cites the unchanged ephemeralMcpCredentialService.ts for completeness of the mandatory-per-brief checklist; that file was not independently re-derived line-by-line in this pass since git diff confirms it is byte-identical to the pre-CH-04 tree.

SEC-09 (audit-log completeness for the mint action) and SC-02/SC-03 (install-script execution and vulnerability-scan visibility for the new redis dependency) were not independently verified against a live audit-log store or an automated scanning tool in this pass; marked UNVERIFIED with LOW confidence/severity rather than PASS.

One MEDIUM, non-blocking finding (LLM-09 / FND-477e4cbf5856): the decide<->act loop bounds tools/call invocations to 8 (CHAT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS) but does not independently bound decide_node's generate_structured call count, which can reach roughly half of LangGraph's recursion_limit=200 if a model keeps re-requesting already-cached (tool, arguments) pairs. Terminates safely (GraphRecursionError -> chat.internal, or the 240s deadline -> chat.timeout); no tenant crossing, no data leak, no retry/redelivery. Recommended as a follow-up ticket, consistent with review.md's independently-recorded Warning 2.
